Docket 1.3.77

**Your reports stay after you quit, and you choose which ones go.**

An audit you ran by hand lived in memory only, so closing Docket lost it — while
a watchlist check had been keeping its report on disk since 1.3.74. The Reports
tab said "audits, kept on this Mac", which was true about privacy and easy to
read as a promise about durability. Now it is both. Every audit is kept
automatically, opens again in full after a relaunch, and stays until you delete
it. Deleting takes two presses, because it cannot be undone.

Nothing is thrown away on your behalf. A cap would be easy and would quietly
lose the one report you meant to keep, so each row shows what it costs on disk
and the decision stays yours. The list of crawled pages is not kept — that is
the part that would fill your disk — and the report says so rather than leaving
it to be discovered.

**The work plan now puts the pages that make you money first.**

The plan ranked by severity, reach and effort, and none of those know that
/pricing sells and /blog/tag/misc does not. A missing title on each ranked
identically. Every one of Docket's checks now ranks a fault higher when it lands
on a page where you sell, book or get enquiries.

It is deliberately too small a nudge to move something past a more serious
problem: a critical issue anywhere still outranks a medium one on your pricing
page. It also only recognises English paths, and it errs towards leaving a page
alone rather than promoting the wrong one.

**Two new checks, both about pages that earn.**

Docket already told you when lots of pages had only one internal link pointing
at them, but stayed quiet if it was only a few — sensible for a tag archive,
wrong for your pricing page. It now names commercial pages that almost nothing
links to.

It also spots pages competing with each other: two pages aiming at the same
search, which split your own links and relevance so neither ranks as well as one
would. These are not duplicates. They are different pages, often written months
apart, which is exactly why they are easy to miss.

**Docket works out what your site is about.**

Topic suggestions used to need you to type in your subject. Docket now reads
what your pages actually say — the words that recur across your titles and
headings — and asks only when it genuinely cannot tell. Monitored sites get
suggestions too, which they never did before.

It will not guess from your web addresses. That was tried, on a bakery whose
address bar mentioned two cities, and it suggested articles about the cities.
When it is not sure, it still asks: a confident wrong subject is worse than a
question.

**And your watchlist says when the change hit the pages that sell.**

A weekly check that reports "3 new issues" is not the same news as "3 new
issues, one of them on your pricing page". Now it tells you which. Sites checked
before this release say nothing on that point rather than guessing, because it
is not something Docket recorded at the time.

99 checks across 13 areas.
